bullets.title: June Jobs Miss: 54k NFP, U-Rate Dips to 4.2%
bullets.body: US nonfarm payrolls came in at a soft 54k for June, well below trend, while the unemployment rate fell to 4.2%. The 3-month average sits at 111k — a meaningful deceleration — adding to the case for Fed easing but also raising growth concerns.

bullets.title: Colombia Central Bank Surprises with 75bp Hike to 12%
bullets.body: Colombia's central bank hiked 75bp to 12% in a split 4-2-1 decision, exceeding the median consensus of 50bp. Fiscal adjustment is expected to set the stage for rate cuts in 2027.

bullets.title: USMCA Won't Get Clean 16-Year Extension; Shifts to Annual Reviews
bullets.body: BofA flags that the July 1 USMCA review will not yield a clean 16-year extension — instead the agreement shifts to annual reviews, remaining in force until 2036 absent a new deal. Ongoing uncertainty is a headwind for cross-border supply chains.

bullets.title: Global REITs +0.8% on the Week; US Multifamily Rent Growth Re-Accelerating
bullets.body: UBS notes global real estate returned +0.8% last week, led by Japan REITs (+1.9%) while Australia lagged (-2.8%). US multifamily asking rents are tracking historical seasonal patterns through June 2026, with indexed rents up 1.7% YTD — a contrast to 2025's June deceleration.

bullets.title: China Property Sales Deteriorating: -12% YoY in June, H1 Down 16%
bullets.body: China's top 100 developers saw contract sales fall 12% YoY in June, a sharp deterioration from -2% in May, bringing H1 2026 down 16% YoY. Singapore residential price growth is easing with 1H26 PPI up only 1.4% YTD.

bullets.title: HK Luxury Retail Surging: +26% YoY in May with Volume Up 10.5%
bullets.body: Hong Kong retail sales rose 7.9% YoY in May, driven by luxury goods up 26% YoY with real volume growth of 10.5% — a standout bright spot in an otherwise soft Asia property/consumer backdrop.

bullets.title: UBS Turns Bullish on European Pharma: Headwinds from Policy/Tariffs/FX Seen Ending
bullets.body: UBS believes the European pharma sector's weakness — driven by policy uncertainty, tariffs, and currency drag — is nearing an end and flags a bullish inflection ahead for the sector.

bullets.title: Starlink Direct-to-Cell: Threat Framed as Complementary, Not Replacement, for Tower Infra
bullets.body: Jefferies is hosting an expert call examining Starlink Direct-to-Cell's impact on tower operators, but preliminary framing suggests LEO satellite networks face technical, regulatory, and cost limitations that limit full terrestrial replacement — a potentially reassuring read for tower stocks.
